title: Minimalist Microwave Rack: Save Kitchen Counter Space with Vertical Storage
excerpt: Complete guide to choosing a minimalist microwave rack to save kitchen counter space. Discover types, materials, ideal sizes, and efficient vertical storage arrangement tips.
content: A microwave is one of the kitchen appliances that takes up quite a bit of space on your kitchen counter. For owners of minimalist kitchens or small kitchens, placing a microwave directly on the work surface means sacrificing valuable food preparation area. **A minimalist microwave rack** is a smart solution to utilize vertical space and free up your kitchen counter.
![Minimalist microwave rack with vertical storage in modern kitchen](/images/blog/rak-microwave.webp)

In this guide, we discuss in detail the various types of microwave racks, how to choose the right size, best materials, and arrangement tips so your kitchen looks neat and functional. Read on for more.

> **Key Takeaways:**
> - Choose products with clear safety labels (food-grade, BPA-free) for daily use
> - Investing slightly more in quality materials (glass, grade 304 stainless steel) saves long-term costs
> - Match sizes to family needs, neither too large nor too small
> - Local marketplaces like Tokopedia, Shopee, and [Sesoris](https://www.sesoris.com/) offer competitive prices with maintained quality
## Why Do You Need a Special Microwave Rack?

A standard microwave has dimensions of approximately 45 x 35 x 30 cm and weighs 10-15 kg. Placing it directly on your kitchen counter means losing almost half a square meter of work space that could be used for chopping vegetables, preparing ingredients, or other cooking activities. For additional information, also see the guide from [The Spruce](https://www.thespruce.com/).

A special microwave rack solves this problem by lifting the microwave to a vertical position, usually above the counter or mounted on the wall. Below or above the microwave, there is still additional space for storing other kitchen equipment. In other words, one vertical area can hold a microwave plus several storage items at the same time.
### Benefits of a Microwave Rack
- **Save counter space** - free up valuable work area in small kitchens
- **Additional storage** - extra shelves below and above the microwave for other equipment
- **Ergonomic position** - microwave placed at eye level for ease of use
- **Better ventilation** - open rack design provides good air circulation for the microwave
- **Neater kitchen appearance** - electronic equipment stored in an organized manner
- **Prevent damage** - microwave safe from water or oil splashes on the counter
## Types of Microwave Racks
![Illustration related to rak microwave](/images/blog/rak-microwave-2.webp)
### 1. Countertop Microwave Stand

This type is placed on top of the kitchen counter with the microwave on the top level and storage shelves below. Although it still takes up counter space, the standing rack maximizes vertical space so the area below the microwave is not wasted. Usually has 2-3 levels. For additional information, also see the guide from [Real Simple](https://www.realsimple.com/).
Its main advantage is ease of installation - no need to drill walls at all. Perfect for renters who cannot damage walls or for those who frequently change kitchen layouts.
### 2. Wall-Mounted Microwave Rack

Mounted on the kitchen wall, this rack completely frees the counter from the microwave's weight. The microwave is placed on a rack that is locked to the wall using thick steel brackets. This type is most effective for saving space but requires a strong wall.
Make sure the wall for installation is made of concrete or brick that can withstand a minimum load of 25-30 kg. Avoid installing on drywall partitions as it could collapse and damage the microwave.
### 3. Over-the-Range Microwave Rack

Designed to be installed directly above the stove, combining the function of a microwave rack with an exhaust fan. This type is very popular in apartments and modern kitchens because it saves a lot of space. However, installation is more complex and usually requires professional service.
### 4. Corner Microwave Rack

Takes advantage of the corner area of the kitchen which is often underutilized. The design adapts to the room's corner shape with the microwave on the main level and additional shelves above or below. A smart choice for small kitchens where every corner needs to be maximized.
### 5. Multifunctional Microwave Rack (Kitchen Baker's Rack)

A tall standing rack with 4-5 levels where one level is specifically designed for the microwave. Other levels can be used to store rice cookers, blenders, toasters, and other kitchen appliances. Perfect for kitchens with many electronic appliances.

## Guide to Choosing the Right Microwave Rack
### 1. Measure Your Microwave Dimensions

The first crucial step is to accurately measure your microwave dimensions. Record the length, width, height, and weight of your microwave. The chosen rack must be at least 5 cm wider and deeper than the microwave dimensions to provide adequate ventilation space.
### 2. Pay Attention to Load Capacity

Standard microwaves weigh 10-15 kg, while larger microwaves can reach 20 kg. Choose a rack with a minimum load capacity of 25 kg per shelf to provide a safety margin. Don't forget to factor in the weight of food that will be heated inside.
### 3. Ensure Adequate Ventilation

Microwaves need good ventilation to prevent overheating. Make sure the rack provides at least 10 cm of empty space at the back and 5 cm on the sides of the microwave. Racks with open design (without closed side walls) are better for air circulation.
### 4. Match the User's Height

The ideal microwave position is at chest to shoulder height for the user. Too high risks spilling hot food when removing it, while too low makes it difficult to see inside the microwave. Consider the height of the family member who uses the microwave most often.
### 5. Check Construction Stability

A microwave rack must be very stable given the considerable weight it bears. Shake the rack before buying - a good rack should not wobble or sway. For wall-mounted racks, make sure the mounting brackets are high quality and installed correctly.

## Tips for Optimal Microwave Rack Organization
After choosing and installing your microwave rack, proper organization will maximize its functionality.
### Hot Zone on Upper Level

Place the microwave and heat-generating appliances (such as toasters or air fryers) on the level with the best ventilation, usually the top level. This prevents heat from being trapped and affecting items on the upper shelf.
### Storage Zone on Lower Level

Use the level below the microwave to store food containers, microwave-safe plates, or spice jars that are frequently used together with the microwave. This arrangement creates an efficient workflow - grab a container, heat it in the microwave, all in one area.
### Utilize Rack Sides
Many microwave racks have open sides where hooks can be installed to hang kitchen towels, spatulas, or other lightweight equipment. Take advantage of every available space.
### Manage Cables Neatly
Dangling microwave cables can be unsightly and dangerous. Use cable organizers or cable clips to tidy up cables behind the rack. Make sure cables are not bent or pinched which could cause damage.
## Common Mistakes to Avoid
- **Choosing a rack that's too tight** - doesn't leave ventilation space around the microwave
- **Installing the rack too high** - risk of accidents when removing hot food
- **Ignoring load capacity** - could cause the rack to bend or collapse
- **Using a weak wall** - for wall-mounted types, drywall is not strong enough
- **Placing near a water source** - water splashes can damage the microwave and cause electrical shorts
- **Not checking if level** - a tilted rack makes the microwave unstable and causes vibration during operation
## Microwave Rack Maintenance
1. **Wipe regularly** - clean the rack surface at least once a week to remove dust and food splatters
2. **Check connections periodically** - tighten bolts that are becoming loose every 1-2 months
3. **Inspect wall brackets** - for wall-mounted racks, make sure brackets are still firmly installed and there are no signs of wall cracks
4. **Avoid overloading** - don't place items exceeding the recommended capacity
5. **Protect the coating** - if the protective layer on the iron rack is scratched, immediately cover it with rust-preventive paint
## Conclusion

A minimalist microwave rack is a very valuable investment for small to medium-sized kitchens. By utilizing vertical storage, you can free your kitchen counter from the microwave's weight while gaining additional storage space for other kitchen equipment.

The key to choosing the right microwave rack is paying attention to microwave dimensions, load capacity, ventilation, and material quality. ## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
Here are answers to the most frequently asked reader questions on this topic.
**Q: How long do quality home organization products typically last?**

With proper routine care, food-grade plastic products last 3-5 years, while borosilicate glass and grade 304 stainless steel can last 10+ years. Key factors are consistent maintenance and avoiding extreme temperature exposure.
**Q: Is this product food-safe?**

Ensure the product is labeled "food-grade" or "BPA-free" before using it for food storage. Safe materials include borosilicate glass, grade 304 stainless steel, and certified food-grade plastic. Avoid plastic without food safety certification, especially for hot or oily foods.
**Q: How do I clean and maintain it?**

Wash with mild dish soap and warm water. Avoid abrasive sponges that can scratch the surface. For stubborn stains, use a baking soda and water paste as a natural cleaner. Dry completely before storing to prevent mold and bacteria.
**Q: What is the price difference between local and imported products?**

Local Indonesian products are typically 30-50% more affordable than imports of similar quality. For daily home organization needs, local products meet the standard. Consider imports only if you need specific features not available in the local market.
